description: Before recommending or setting up one open-source project: check it against the user's limits (no GPU, arm64, RAM, permissive license only, no outside services, Docker) fact by fact, with a verdict; the start command pinned to a release, variable names and ports; known pitfalls (review weaknesses, score penalties, stale releases, security advisories, failed safety checks, copyleft terms); what in its review matches the use case; and up to 3 projects in its category that fit better. From Archestack's (archestack.com) checked facts, not the project's own marketing. Use it after recommend_stack or whenever the user is about to adopt a named project for a specific job; it never installs or runs anything.

arm64.description: true: it must run on arm64 (Apple Silicon, Graviton)

docker.description: true: it must ship Docker files

no_gpu.description: true: the machine has no GPU

no_outside_services.description: true: it must run without outside services (hosted APIs, a separate database)

permissive_only.description: true: only MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD and similar licenses are allowed

project.description: Project id like "best-of-ai/qdrant", a GitHub repo like "qdrant/qdrant", or a name like "Qdrant"

ram_gb.description: RAM the machine has, in GB

use_case.description: What the user wants to do with it, to match against its strengths and weaknesses

name: how_to_apply
title: Check a project against the user's limits
